target_customer: Hospitals, health centers, home health organizations, telehealth programs and clinics that pay for interpretation services for non-English speaking patients
problem: Providers wait for human interpreters or use slow phone and video services when treating patients who do not speak English, which delays care and costs hospitals large sums each year.
business_model: B2B SaaS and usage-based AI interpretation sold to provider organizations as a replacement for per-minute human interpretation services
product_category: Healthcare voice AI, real-time speech-to-speech medical interpretation

founders.name: Alex Mehregan
prior_employers: Apple (software engineer on Apple Intelligence and the updated Siri, per YC page)
previous_startups: Described on the YC page as a 2x founder; earlier startups not named
founders.background_notes: Source is the YC company page.

competitors.name: GLOBO Language Solutions (GLOBO KAI)
competitors.what: AI interpreter offered to healthcare provider sites, mainly for administrative settings
competitors.traction_then: Made available to 3,000 provider sites in June 2025 after an early 2025 pilot

competitors.name: Artisight
competitors.what: Voice-activated interpreters added to its smart hospital platform, compatible with any translation service
competitors.traction_then: Launched July 2025 inside an existing hospital platform

competitors.name: Vocality Health
competitors.what: Instant AI medical language interpretation for hospitals, a YC Winter 2025 company
competitors.traction_then: Not stated in the sources opened

competitors.name: No Barrier
competitors.what: AI medical interpreter with low-latency speech models and compliance guardrails
competitors.traction_then: Vendor claims connection in under 30 seconds and 30+ languages
competitors.funding_then: A directory item reports a 2.7M USD seed, unverified

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time speech-to-speech translation in 150+ languages with medical accuracy, a monitoring layer for meaning changes, and EHR integration are hard for a three-person team, although foundation speech models were available in 2025.

defensibility.rationale: Several startups and incumbents shipped similar AI interpreters in 2025. Differentiation rests on accuracy tooling (the Guardian monitor) and EHR integrations, which take time to copy but are not structural.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: As of early 2026 incumbent interpretation vendors were adding AI products (GLOBO KAI in June 2025); no acquisition of Opalite is reported.

market_need_then: Hospitals pay per minute for human phone and video interpreters, with long waits at the point of care. The company's own site cites one customer that halved interpretation costs. Demand from the AI interpreter wave of 2025 is visible in multiple launches.

branding.domain_note: Uses opalitehealth.com, a prefix-plus-word domain, not the exact .com.

identity.logo: Not described by any source opened
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and credibility focused, stresses safety, compliance and accuracy

rebrands.why: An App Store listing titled Opalite (Formerly Calliope) and the website footer naming Calliope AI Inc. suggest a rename; the date and reason are not sourced.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself, only directory listings and a trademark application filed April 2026. Too early to show brand pull.

outcome_analysis: Opalite is an active Winter 2026 company with no exit and no confirmed funding round. Its path depends on whether hospital buyers trust AI interpretation more than human services, on accuracy tooling, and on competition from several startups and incumbents that launched AI interpreters in 2025. Too early for a verdict.
notes: Funding unverified: a search summary cited about 700K USD seed led by YC and Forum Ventures from a California Health Care Foundation report, and a jobs directory lists 745K USD seed; neither source was opened, so no round is recorded. Cathleen Kuo, a physician, is named on the YC page as a company contact with a personal story but is not listed as an active founder, so she is not recorded as a co-founder. One profile lists Palo Alto and others San Francisco. The Calliope link comes from an App Store title and website footer only.
